regions.region: page 1 title, author block, abstract, keywords, and article metadata
regions.finding: Verified the source title and aggregate asymmetric-allenylation claim. No experiment-specific quantities or yields occur in this region.

regions.region: page 1 Figure 1A–B
regions.finding: Figure 1 illustrates chirality classes and example natural/product allenes. It is chemical context, not a reaction scheme or current-paper experiment.

regions.region: page 1 introduction and discussion of Scheme 1A/B
regions.finding: The text attributes paths a–h and earlier allene-asymmetrization methods to references 12–26; they are represented as literature examples, not current-paper experiments.

regions.region: page 1 Scheme 1C introduction and start of Results and Discussion
regions.finding: The text introduces the current generic double-control reaction and the initial racemic 1a/2a optimization. Experiment-specific rows appear on page 2 and are linked there rather than duplicated.

unresolved: Figure 1 natural-product structures were not treated as reaction participants.
Generic Scheme 1 structures do not define unique compounds or experiment-specific yields.

regions.region: page 2 upper-left Scheme 1A
regions.finding: Paths a–h are a compact prior-literature survey. They remain one literature-context record and are not expanded into current-paper experiments.

regions.region: page 2 middle-left Scheme 1B and Scheme 1C
regions.finding: Scheme 1B contains two prior allene-asymmetrization arrows; Scheme 1C is the generic current double-control reaction. No row yield is assigned to these generic arrows.

regions.region: page 2 upper-right Table 1 entries 1–9 and footnotes
regions.finding: Nine separate optimization runs were extracted with ligand, time, substrate recovery, NMR yield, d.r., signed/source ee, shared charges, solvent/temperature, and analytical bases. Entry 9 uses anhydrous K2CO3/NMP at 30 °C and remains distinct from Table 2 entry 1.

regions.region: page 2 optimization and scope narrative
regions.finding: The narrative supplies the 500 °C/8 h K2CO3 preparation statement, identifies Table 2 scope and its independent gram-scale entry 10, and links X-ray assignment of 3da. The 8 h statement conflicts with page-4 General Information's 6 h statement and both are retained.

regions.region: page 2 Figure 2 ORTEP
regions.finding: ORTEP characterizes Table 2 product (Ra,S)-3da. It is not a second preparation and does not verify a machine structure encoding.

regions.region: page 2 lower-right discussion of opposite ligand and cooperative/stereoisomer controls
regions.finding: The prose introduces Table 3 and Scheme 2 experiments shown on page 3. Those rows/arrows are represented once with cross-page evidence.

unresolved: Anhydrous K2CO3 preparation time conflicts: 8 h here versus 6 h on page 4.
Most scope/control operations omit workup and isolated mass in the main text.

regions.region: page 3 upper-left Table 2 entries 1–16 and footnotes
regions.finding: Sixteen distinct (R)-L8 scope runs were extracted. The ordinary and 1 g-scale 3hc runs remain separate; entry 1 is linked to the detailed page-4/5 procedure. Shared d.r. >99:1, isolated yields, ee, exact standard charges, and row times are retained.

regions.region: page 3 lower-left Table 3 entries 1–6 and footnotes
regions.finding: Six distinct (S)-L8 scope runs were extracted with shared charges, row times, isolated yields, d.r., and ee. They are not merged with analogous (R)-L8 runs.

regions.region: page 3 upper-right Scheme 2A equations 4–5
regions.finding: Two distinct cooperative-effect controls (1q and 1r) were extracted with separate times, products, yields, and ee values.

regions.region: page 3 center-right Scheme 2B equations 6–9
regions.finding: Four stereoisomer-specific 1h reactions were extracted separately, including starting d.r./ee and product-specific yield/d.r./ee; low-yield mismatched runs retain the stated unidentified byproducts as unresolved.

regions.region: page 3 lower-right Scheme 3 and mechanistic prose
regions.finding: E,E-eta1-dienyl Pd and syn-eta3-Int A are proposed intermediates in the authors' rationale, not isolated preparations. The cited separate SI molecular model was not associated or imported.

unresolved: Table 2 entry 10 does not print exact gram-scale charges or NMP volume.
Scheme 2 arrows omit absolute scale, operational workup, isolated mass, and several measurement bases.
The separate SI molecular model is unavailable and was not inferred.

regions.region: page 4 upper-left completion of Scheme 3 discussion
regions.finding: The text completes the proposed stereochemical rationale and refers to a separate SI computational model. This is mechanism context, not an additional experiment or SI association.

regions.region: page 4 middle-left Scheme 4 equations 10–12
regions.finding: Three independent kinetic-resolution experiments were extracted with substrate 1:1 d.r., ligand enantiomer, nucleophile/base equivalents, temperature/time, isolated yield, isolated and crude d.r. statements, and ee. Equation 11's crude d.r. is explicitly not determinable by NMR.

regions.region: page 4 upper-right Scheme 5 arrows a–f and condition footnote
regions.finding: Six distinct synthetic applications were extracted. Arrows c and f retain ordered two-stage operations; arrow a retains the printed 0 °C-to-room-temperature 3 h transition; product-specific yield, ee, and E/Z outcomes are linked to products.

regions.region: page 4 conclusions and General Information
regions.finding: General Information supplies materials handling and states K2CO3 was heated at 500 °C for 6 h, conflicting with page 2's 8 h statement. Conclusions add no new experiment.

regions.region: page 4 lower-right beginning of Typical Procedure for Table 2 entry 1
regions.finding: The detailed 3aa procedure begins with exact catalyst/ligand/base charges, glove-box charging, 5 mL NMP, nitrogen atmosphere, 30 °C/30 min preactivation, substrate solution and nucleophile addition, then 30 °C/12 h. It enriches Table 2 entry 1 rather than creating a duplicate.

unresolved: K2CO3 preparation time remains conflicting between pages 2 and 4.
Scheme 4/5 omit absolute scale and most workups/purifications.
The page-4 Typical Procedure continues onto page 5.

regions.region: page 5 upper-left completion of Typical Procedure and 3aa characterization
regions.finding: The existing Table 2 entry 1 was completed with brine washes, Et2O extraction, Na2SO4 drying, 8:1 chromatography, 0.3965 g/77% product, 96% ee, and full HPLC basis. Characterization does not create another experiment.

regions.region: page 5 Supporting Information statement
regions.finding: The article states online SI availability, but no SI file is explicitly associated in source_mapping.json; no SI-only fact was imported.

regions.region: page 5 acknowledgment
regions.finding: Yang Tang is thanked for reproducing Table 3 entry 2. Because no independent charges, conditions, outcome, or run identifier are supplied, this is provenance on the existing record and not a duplicate run.

regions.region: page 5 references 1–37
regions.finding: Bibliography/prior-literature context only; external papers were not expanded into current-paper experiments.

regions.region: page 5 footnote 29 crystal data and CCDC 1537642
regions.finding: Crystal data characterize existing Table 2 product (Ra,S)-3da. The deposition is not a preparation, not an associated SI file, and not machine-structure verification.

unresolved: SI association remains unestablished despite the availability statement.
The reproduction acknowledgment does not define a separable run.
CCDC 1537642 does not verify a machine structure encoding.
